headline: Mariana has lost 8% of her body weight (77.9 kg to 71.7 kg) between Sep 5 and Nov 24, 2026, and her son and caregiver Marcus has asked for respite.

items.statement: Weight fell at each reading in the review period: 77.9 kg on Sep 5, 75.7 kg on Oct 1, 73.6 on Oct 28 and 71.7 on Nov 24, 2026. That is 6.2 kg (8%) in about 11 weeks. On Nov 24 the dietitian recorded poor appetite, skipped breakfasts, and about 50% of day center lunches eaten.
items.verifier_note: The weights match the vitals record. The 6.2 kg (8%) loss matches, and Sep 5 to Nov 24 is about 11 weeks. The dietitian note supports the appetite, breakfast and 50% lunch details.

items.statement: A Nov 26 late-entry note says the weight loss actually happened on Jul 16, 2026 and was discussed at the last review. The vitals record shows 77.9 kg on Jul 14 and at every reading through Sep 5, with the decline starting after that. The note conflicts with the structured weights.
items.verifier_note: The Nov 26 late entry gives Jul 16 as the date of the loss and says it was discussed at the last review. The vitals show 77.9 kg on Jul 14 and at every reading through Sep 5, so the conflict is accurately described.

items.statement: The dietitian's plan from Nov 24 includes an oral nutrition supplement twice daily, weekly weights, and a dental check for chewing problems. No supplement appears in the active medication list, and no encounters are recorded in the period, so the team may want to confirm the plan is under way.
items.verifier_note: The plan items match the Nov 24 note, and the encounters list is empty. The medications record only shows nothing started or stopped since Sep 1. It does not include an active medication list, so the claim that no supplement appears there is not directly supported.

items.statement: On Sep 27, 2026 Marcus, her son and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group. The notes in this period do not show an outcome.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 27 social work note supports every detail. It records no outcome.

questions_for_team: Which date is correct for the weight loss? The late entry says Jul 16, but the vitals record shows 77.9 kg through Sep 5 and a steady decline afterward.
The PCP notes of Sep 2, Sep 27 and Nov 27 say chronic conditions are stable. Has the PCP reviewed the weight trend?
Has the supplement started, and who is doing the weekly weights and arranging the dental check?
What respite or evening support can be put in place for Marcus, and has he followed up on the support group?
Does Marcus's strain or evening coverage affect Mariana's meals and appetite at home?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and that the last IDT review date and prior plan of care are on file before comparing changes.
Falls and near-falls in the window: count, circumstances, injuries, and any post-fall assessment. Relevant given age 81 and osteoporosis (fracture risk).
ED visits and hospital admissions in the window: reason, discharge summary, and whether any follow-up appointments or medication changes resulted.
Cardiac symptoms: chest pain or angina episodes, use of PRN nitroglycerin spray (count and frequency), dyspnea, palpitations, edema, and any cardiology visits, given ischemic heart disease.

Medication reconciliation: confirm the four active medications (metoprolol succinate, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin, vitamin B12 injection) and check for any starts, stops, or dose changes in the window, including new antihypertensives, diabetes agents, or antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy not on the list.
Vitamin B12 injection schedule: verify doses were given on time and that the B12 indication and last level are documented, given long-standing anemia history.

Diabetes and glycemic data: HbA1c, fasting and random glucose trend, hypoglycemia events, and whether glucose-lowering therapy is documented, given type 2 diabetes with diabetic kidney disease and a medication list that contains no diabetes agent.

Kidney function: most recent eGFR and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio, creatinine trend, and whether results were reviewed, given CKD stage 1 labeled alongside diabetic kidney disorder (verify staging consistency).

Blood pressure and lipid data: BP readings across the window against the care-plan target, and lipid panel (triglycerides, LDL) since simvastatin 20 mg and hypertriglyceridemia history; note whether statin intensity has been reviewed.
Weight and BMI trend (obesity, BMI 30+ on record), plus hemoglobin/CBC trend given anemia history; flag unintentional weight change, appetite changes, or dietary concerns.

Function and ADLs/IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, meal preparation, medication management; mobility aids; cognition screen results and any mood screen (e.g., PHQ) and social engagement or attendance at PACE center or day programming.
Caregiver and social situation: any change in living arrangement, caregiver availability or strain, transportation barriers, and advance directive or healthcare proxy status.

Care-plan items due in or near the window: scheduled assessments, immunizations, osteoporosis treatment review or bone density follow-up, eye and foot exams for diabetes, and any outstanding referrals. Flag each as done, overdue, or not documented for the IDT to discuss.
